The body art shows real material behaviour: the paint is a thin matte water-based coat laid on with visible brush strokes and tiny pigment ridges, her skin texture, pores and fine hairs still visible through the thin paint, the pattern following the curves of her bra and hips, a soft natural shadow around the line between the breasts, her skin tone running naturally everywhere else. Face: her face is bare of any garment — real living flesh with real pores, a soft sheen of natural oils and bright real catchlights, the face of a real Black woman with strong, striking features, a broad nose and full lips, an unmistakably feminine face with a calm, composed expression, makeup: large round eyes with bright real catchlights, thick curled lashes with drawn-on lower lashes, soft pink and lilac eyeshadow, round pink blush, glossy cherry-pink lips.

Background: a small square room whose two facing side walls and ceiling are floor-to-ceiling mirrors, with a polished black floor, so that her reflections repeat to infinity on both sides: her profile, her back and her three-quarter view appear in a long receding tunnel of identical figures wearing the same body art and the same towering heels, each one a little smaller and dimmer than the last, with warm pin lights along the ceiling edge glowing in the repeating frames, lit by soft warm light with gentle shadows. ONE woman only. Three-quarter-length shot from the top of her head down to just above her knees, the camera at chest height standing well back in the room so the mirror walls stay widely visible on both sides and her reflections run large and clear. This is one single photograph taken with one camera at one moment, the reflections being part of that same photograph, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/5.6, realistic photographic grain, a real photograph. 8K portrait 2:3 aspect ratio.
